subject: body
title: Head to Toe
about: Naming the parts of the body from head to toe and where each one is: head, neck, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hands and fingers, chest, tummy, back, hip, knee, ankle, heel, feet and toes, plus higher and lower, left and right, and how many fingers and toes. Body-part names are not a Grade 1 objective of their own in NC's Healthful Living standards, so this is a bridge topic tagged to the closest codes, 1.PCH.1.4 (dressing the right parts for the weather) and 1.PCH.2.1 (keeping those parts safe from injury). Read it together and let him touch each part as the card names it.
tip: Play Simon Says with the parts in this deck: Simon says touch your wrist, your heel, your left shoulder.

cards.q: Which part of your body is at the very top?
cards.note: Your head holds your brain, eyes, ears, nose and mouth. Hats go here.

cards.q: What holds your head up and lets it turn from side to side?
cards.note: Your neck joins your head to your body. Nod yes and shake no to feel it work.

cards.q: Where does your arm join your body, up at the top?
cards.note: Shrug and your shoulders go up. A backpack rests on them.

cards.q: What bends in the middle of your arm?
cards.note: Bend your elbow to bring your hand up to your mouth. Cough into it, too.

cards.q: What bends between your hand and your arm?
cards.note: A watch sits on your wrist. Wave and feel it bend.

cards.q: Count the fingers and thumbs on two hands. How many do most people have?
cards.note: Five on each hand. Two hands make ten, so you can count to ten on them.

cards.q: What is the front of your body between your neck and your tummy?
cards.note: Your heart and lungs are inside your chest. Feel it rise when you breathe in.

cards.q: What is the soft front part of your body, under your chest?
cards.note: Grown-ups also say belly. Your stomach, where food goes, is inside it.

cards.q: You lie down on it. It runs behind you from your shoulders to your hips. What is it?
cards.note: Your backbone runs down the middle of your back. Sit up tall to keep it happy.

cards.q: Where does your leg join your body?
cards.note: Put your hands on your hips. Each leg swings from a hip.

cards.q: What bends in the middle of your leg?
cards.note: Knees bend when you sit, run and jump. Knee pads keep them safe when you skate.

cards.q: What joins your foot to your leg?
cards.note: Your sock folds over your ankle. Circle your foot to feel it move.

cards.q: What is the back part of your foot called, under your ankle?
cards.note: Your heel touches the ground first when you walk. Shoes have a heel too.

cards.q: How many toes do most people have on one foot?
cards.note: Five toes on each foot. The big toe helps you balance.

cards.q: You stand up straight. Which part of your body is lowest, touching the floor?
cards.note: Head at the top, feet at the bottom. That is head to toe.

cards.q: Which is higher up on your body, your shoulder or your knee?
cards.note: Shoulders are up near your head. Knees are down near the floor.

cards.q: You put a hand on your heart. Your heart is a little to which side?
cards.note: Your heart sits in the middle of your chest, tipped a little to the left.

cards.q: Hold your hands up, backs toward your face. Which hand's thumb and pointer make a letter L?
cards.note: L is for left. The right hand makes a backwards L.
